description: "Use when a check, test run or pipeline you were given has failed."
---
<!-- Generated by Pixl from the skill "Fix a failing check", version 1. Edit it in the Skills tab, not here: changes made here are overwritten. -->

## Steps
1. Read the end of the failing output. Copy the first error line.
2. Run the same command yourself and see it fail.
3. Write one cause in one line.
4. Make the smallest change in the code that removes that cause.
5. Run the same command again.
6. If it still fails, go back to step 3 with the new output. After three tries stop and report what you saw.
7. Run the whole test command once.
## Checklist
- [ ] The command that failed now exits 0.
- [ ] No test, Dockerfile, CI file or setting was changed to make it pass.
- [ ] The change is small.
## Definition of done
The exact command that failed now passes in this run, and you quoted its summary line.
## Verify
Re-run the exact failing command, then the whole test command.
## Common mistakes
- Weakening or skipping the test: fix the code.
- Fixing a different problem than the one in the output.
- Guessing without reproducing it first.
- Editing build or CI files: they are held back and a person must look.
## Example
Output: `AssertionError: 6 != 3` in `test_average`. Cause: `average` divides by `len - 1`. Fix: divide by `len`. Run `python -m pytest -q`: `2 passed`.
